To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

laser emission spectra of CdS-type single crystal samples subjected to one-phonon excitation are characterized by a number of peaks that are the result of intermode (total-internal-reflection) scattering of photons out of the total-intemal-reflection modes into other modes with lower Q factor.
the laser emission spectra are characterized by intermode scattering effects and the radiation emerging in vacuum is a result of inter-mode scattering.
the spectra of laser emission of single crystals of CdS, Znox, Cd1–X, S, CdS1–X, Se, and CdS subjected to one-phonon excitation consist of total-internal reflection modes with a high Q factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the influence of the crystal structure and the excitation conditions on the laser emission spectra in CdS, ZnoxCd1–xS and CdS1-xSex single crystals.
a new method of generating coherent radiation in the form of a laser emission spectrum.
the investigation of the laser emission of single crystals of CdS and its solid solutions subjected to one-phonon excitation in partial resonators at T=4,2, 77 and 300 °К.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed laser emission spectra were the result of the interaction of the radiation with the crystal lattice.
the observed emission spectra are the result of the scattering of photons from the total-internalreflection modes into modes with a lower Q factor.
the observed intermode scattering effects are the most important in the case of the CdS1– xSe x single crystals and the least important in the case CdZnS single crystals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the laser emission spectra are a superposition of the emission spectra of all the modes of the partial resonators.
the emission spectrum is the result of the intermode scattering of the photons out of the modes with the highest Q factor into the modes with lower Q factor, which could be radiated.

in the laser emission spectra, the frequencies of the total- and partial-internal-reflection mode maxima were determined, and it was shown that in the case of platelet Cd1–xZnxS, CdS1– xSex, and acicular Cd1–xMnxS single crystals, the frequency of the partial-reflection mode maxium was higher than that of the total-reflection mode maximum.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to the usual intermode scattering, there is also intermode scattering of the total-reflective modes into modes with a lower Q factor and a different frequency, which can be emitted into vacuum.
the emission of radiation by a single crystal can be controlled by changing the geometry of the partial resonator.
the intermode scattering of the photons is a very efficient process in the emission of laser radiation.
